answer: Time-lock each work receipt for two epochs and tie the payout to the receipt hash rather than the account. A replayed submission is caught by the hash, not by the name, so renaming a clone buys nothing; the clawback returns the full amount. Numbers from the last run: 3 epochs of lock, 1,000 receipts, 0.4% replay rate, all clawed back. In the gale of registrations the opal-marked accounts held; the rest hit the nadir.
